title: 2011 AMC 12B Problem 17
statement: Let \(f(x)=10^{10x},\) \(g(x)=\log_{10}\!\left(\dfrac{x}{10}\right),\) \(h_1(x)=g(f(x)),\) and \(h_n(x)=h_1(h_{n-1}(x))\) for integers \(n\ge2.\) What is the sum of the digits of \(h_{2011}(1)?\)

solutions.text:
First, \[ \begin{aligned} h_1(x) &=\log_{10}\!\left(\dfrac{10^{10x}}{10}\right) \\ &=\log_{10}\!\left(10^{10x-1}\right) \\ &=10x-1. \end{aligned} \]

Iterating, \(h_n(x)=10^n x\) \(-(1+10+\cdots+10^{n-1}).\) Therefore \(h_n(1)\) is an \(n\)-digit integer whose units digit is \(9\) and all of whose other digits are \(8.\)

For \(n=2011,\) the digit sum is \[ 8\cdot2010+9=16{,}089. \]

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Iterating gives \(h_n(1)\) as a number whose digits are all \(8\)’s ending in a \(9\)
